Distinguished from the more common word for 'prince' (nasi), this term appears primarily in poetic texts and refers to defeated enemy leaders or foreign rulers. The contexts involve military defeat and judgment: Midianite kings defeated by Israel, princes of the north brought low, rulers of Edom in Ezekiel's oracle. The term may carry connotations of established, hereditary leadership over defined territories or peoples, particularly non-Israelite rulers."
